title: Article 302 — Power of Parliament to impose restrictions on trade, commerce and intercourse

content.overview: Article 302 empowers Parliament by law to impose such restrictions on the freedom of trade, commerce or intercourse between one State and another or within any part of the territory of India as may be required in the public interest.
content.glance: Parliament may by law restrict trade/commerce/intercourse (inter-State or within any part of India) in the public interest.
content.study:
Article 302 parliamentary restriction power:
- Scope: freedom of trade, commerce or intercourse between States or within any part of India.
- Standard: as may be required in the **public interest**.
- Instrument: law made by Parliament.

Broader than State power under Article 304; not limited to non-discriminatory taxes or reasonable restrictions in the same way as 304, but must still meet public interest and other constitutional constraints.

Examination: Parliament only; public interest; inter-State or intra-territory; contrast Art 304.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: Parliament may by law impose restrictions on trade, commerce or intercourse between States or within any part of India as required in the public interest.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What power does Parliament have under Article 302?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 302 empowers Parliament by law to impose such restrictions on the freedom of trade, commerce or intercourse between one State and another or within any part of the territory of India as may be required in the public interest.

examTips: Parliamentary restrictions in public interest; inter-State or within India.

keyTakeaways: Art 302: Parliament may restrict trade/commerce in public interest.
